clue.text: Sausage — small amount — more's consumed — entirety knocked back

indicators.note: what is consumed is swallowed up, so one piece ends up inside another

parts.note: a tad is a tiny bit

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is downed, but read literally it is sent backwards, so the letters run in reverse

explanation.surface: A disjointed shopping note about a sausage, a little more eaten, and the whole thing knocked back.
explanation.walkthrough: The dashes split the clue into separate instructions rather than a sentence, and 'knocked back' sounds like drinking but turns a word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Mortadella is a large Italian cured pork sausage from Bologna, studded with cubes of fat.

clue.text: Semi-solid extract?

indicators.note: an extract is a portion taken out of something larger, here out of the run of letters

explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across the join in 'Semi-solid', and the whole clue also describes the paste, so wordplay and definition are one.
explanation.definitionFit: Miso is a thick fermented soybean paste, a semi-solid product drawn from beans and used as seasoning in Japanese cooking.

clue.text: Meet people

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sporting meeting or contest of speed
second meaning: a group sharing descent, a nation or ethnic group

explanation.walkthrough: 'Meet people' reads as a verb phrase about socialising, but 'Meet' is the noun for an athletics event.
explanation.definitionFit: An athletics meet is a sporting competition, as a race is; a race is also a group of humans with shared ancestry.

clue.text: Rather than pose, Pa stood awkwardly

indicators.note: done awkwardly means done clumsily and out of order, so the letters come out jumbled

explanation.surface: Father, asked to strike a pose for a photo, just stood there stiffly instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rather than' looks like it begins the sentence, but it is the definition; all eleven letters of the rest are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases introduce an alternative being set aside or contrasted, in preference to or instead of something.

clue.text: Gives power to Lebanese, endlessly in revolution

indicators.note: a revolution overturns the established order, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement
without an end means the final letter is cut off

explanation.surface: Political commentary: someone is empowering the Lebanese while the country is in upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' tempts a reversal, but turning the letters round gives nonsense; it means upheaval, a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To enable is to make able or empower, granting someone the authority or means to act.

clue.text: Fallen angel's striking if cruel

indicators.note: striking can mean remarkable or eye-catching, and also hitting something hard enough to knock it out of shape

explanation.surface: A fallen angel is remarkably handsome despite being cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' reads as an adjective, 'good-looking', but it signals the rearrangement of the two short words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Christian tradition Lucifer is the name of the angel cast out of heaven, later identified with Satan.

clue.text: Put a little design on one cake's exterior?

definitions.text: Put a little design on one cake's exterior?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: only a little of the word is used, its opening letter
the exterior of a word is its outside, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Decorating a cake by adding a small pattern to its outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts the little bit of design after one and the cake's shell; the whole clue also describes decorating a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice a cake is to coat its outside with sugary topping, often piped into decorative patterns.

clue.text: Singer's credit test declined

indicators.note: to decline a word in grammar is to change its form, so the letters take a new shape

explanation.surface: A pop singer failed a credit check when applying for a loan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' is a songbird, a standard crossword trick: no musician is involved.
explanation.definitionFit: The crested tit is a small European songbird with a pointed crest, and birds that sing are called singers in crosswords.

clue.text: I look just like someone: Quasimodo, famously

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an exact double of another person
second meaning, read literally: a bell-ringer who has died

explanation.walkthrough: Quasimodo is the bell-ringer of Notre-Dame in Victor Hugo's novel, and he dies at the end, so he is a ringer who is dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead ringer is an idiom for someone who resembles another person exactly; the phrase is also taken literally here.

clue.text: Respected Costa Ricans abandoning island for resort

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, putting the letters into a different order
to abandon something is to leave it behind, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: I is the standard abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Well-regarded Costa Ricans leave their island for a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' reads as a holiday spot but splits into re-sort; with one I removed, the rest is reshuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sacrosanct is regarded as too important or holy to be challenged, so it is highly respected.

clue.text: In retirement, dined on fine cheese

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw or go back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to dine is to eat; past tense
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A pensioner enjoys good cheese for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the first piece after the second before the whole is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a white brined Greek curd product made from sheep's or goat's milk.

clue.text: Dessert platter, ripe piece of fruit prepared

indicators.note: ingredients prepared are worked into something new, so the letters are rearranged
a piece is just a small bit, the opening letter

explanation.surface: A dessert course: a platter with a ripe piece of fruit prepared on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece of fruit' looks like it means an apple, which is tempting given the answer, but it supplies only one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple fritter is a sweet made of battered and deep-fried slices of the orchard crop, eaten as a pudding.

clue.text: Physicist contains awe in congregation

indicators.note: a congregation is a gathering, and gathered letters can be assembled in any order

explanation.surface: A scientist inspires wonder among a church gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contains' looks like a container signal, but it is simply part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Isaac Newton was the English scientist who formulated the laws of motion and universal gravitation.

clue.text: Mariner's heading to Egypt, a piece of headgear covered in blotchy marking

indicators.note: whatever is covered has something wrapped all around it, so it ends up enclosed

parts.note: a stain is a discoloured mark

indicators.note: a heading is what goes at the top, so the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: A sailor sets off for Egypt wearing a hat covered in stains.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letter, A and the hat go together inside STAIN, splitting it after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea captain is the master of a ship, and a mariner is any sailor or seafarer.

clue.text: Interdenominational material welcoming trendy (essentially smug) church offered up

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised up means read from the bottom, so the letters run backwards
to welcome is to take someone in, so one piece goes inside another
the essence of a word is its core, the letters at its centre

parts.note: the middle two letters of smug
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Fabric for a mixed-faith service is presented by a self-satisfied, fashionable church.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'offered up' means read from the bottom. CE, the Church of England, is the usual crossword church, and the brackets hold just one stray piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecumenical describes cooperation between different Christian churches, so it means involving several denominations.

clue.text: Indulgences lapsed Catholic applies?

parts.note: a lapsed member is a former one, an ex
C is the abbreviation for Catholic
to apply something is to use it

explanation.surface: A Catholic who has stopped practising makes use of indulgences.
explanation.walkthrough: Indulgences in Catholic doctrine are remissions of punishment for sin; the whole clue suggests the justifications a lapsed believer offers.
explanation.definitionFit: Excuses are pardons or reasons offered to be let off, and indulgences grant release from penalty, so the two overlap.

clue.text: Scampered round pale Dutch national

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so one piece encloses others

parts.note: to scamper is to run quickly
D is the abbreviation for Dutch

explanation.surface: A pallid Dutchman dashes round in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch national' looks like the definition, a person from the Netherlands, but Dutch only gives a letter and the definition is 'national' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen of a country, and a Rwandan is a citizen of Rwanda in central Africa.

clue.text: Welcome dictionaries' inclusion of 'LOLsome'?

indicators.note: something included is held within, so the letters lie inside the phrase

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Dictionaries ought to welcome a newly coined internet word into their pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welcome' reads as an exclamation of approval, but it supplies most of the letters. LOL is internet slang for laughing out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: 'LOLsome' is a made-up word for laugh-provoking, and the question mark flags this invented synonym for funny.

clue.text: '70s film Taxi Driver abrasive, ultimately capturing a time

indicators.note: to capture is to take prisoner and hold inside, so one piece goes within another
ultimately means at the end, so the final letters are taken

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A film critic finds the 1970s film Taxi Driver harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taxi Driver' is italicised as a film title, tempting it as the answer, but Taxi gives CAB and Driver only its last letter. CABRE captures A, then T follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabaret is the 1972 musical film starring Liza Minnelli, set in a Berlin nightclub.

clue.text: Lapse in rule after year's end

parts.note: December is the final month of the year, abbreviated DEC
to rule is to draw a straight line

explanation.surface: A lapse in the rules that happens after the end of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the month first; DEC is the calendar abbreviation for December.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse can mean a gradual falling off or deterioration, which is a decline in standards or condition.

clue.text: Spooner's chosen a time for collection of information

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously mixed up the opening sounds of words, so the sounds swap places

parts.note: to choose a time is to fix an appointment; swapping the sounds of the two key words produces the result

explanation.surface: Someone has picked a moment to gather together some information.
explanation.walkthrough: The swap here moves whole syllables rather than just opening consonants: SET A DATE becomes 'date a set'.
explanation.definitionFit: A data set is a structured collection of related records or values, the raw material of statistics and analysis.

clue.text: In France, having tucked into bean tart, you'll get something to drink

indicators.note: to tuck into is to slip inside, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: a pinto is a mottled kidney bean
F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: A visitor in France tucks into a bean tart and is rewarded with a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' suggests eating, but it means placing F between the two words. Bitter is a British style of hoppy draught beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pint of bitter is a pub measure of British ale, a classic beverage ordered at the bar.

clue.text: Here you see outsized competitors hover excitingly, primarily?

definitions.text: Here you see outsized competitors hover excitingly, primarily?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letters are used

parts.note: the opening letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A scene of big players hovering tensely at a line in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes darts: heavyweight players stand at the line, hovering before the throw. The oche is the darts throwing line, a British pub-game term.
explanation.definitionFit: The oche is the line behind which a darts player stands, where large competitors famously hover before throwing.

clue.text: Surreptitious announcement: 'May I also say: good man'

parts.note: PS, postscript, introduces an afterthought in a letter
a saint is a good man, abbreviated ST

explanation.surface: Someone whispers a secret aside: 'May I add, you're a good fellow.'
explanation.walkthrough: ST for saint, a good man, is a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The interjection is used to attract attention quietly or secretly, a hushed call rather than a public statement.

clue.text: Knowing what's between heel and toes

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slyly playful, mischievously aware
second meaning: the curved underside of the foot

explanation.walkthrough: 'Knowing' looks like a verb, but it is the adjective, as in a knowing look.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch smile is a knowing, teasing one; the foot's arch is the raised curve of the sole midway along.

clue.text: Practical information announced, underwear in piles

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so we go by how the words sound

parts.note: piles are stacks; the S slides across the word break when spoken

explanation.surface: Useful advice delivered alongside heaps of lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piles' might suggest a medical complaint, but it just means heaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting down to brass tacks means dealing with the basic practical facts and essential details of a matter.

clue.text: Infielder regularly gets a flower

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A baseball infielder is regularly given a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' in crosswords is often something that flows, a river, rather than a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A river flows, so it is a crossword 'flow-er', and the Nile is Africa's great waterway.

clue.text: Losing train of thought visiting Australian bronzed fella

parts.note: visiting a place is being at it
A is the abbreviation for Australian

explanation.surface: Someone distracted while staying with a sun-bronzed Aussie bloke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bronzed' gives just the colour, a short word, rather than the whole descriptive phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Going off at a tangent is an idiom for drifting suddenly onto an unrelated subject mid-conversation.
